_about: What the pitch deck says in auto-play (/slides?narrate=1): per slide, one line per reveal step. Index 0 plays when the slide opens, index N after the Nth tap. An empty line is a silent beat. Record with scripts/make-deck-narration.js.
cover: Déjà Vu isn't a chatbot. It's a memory layer any personal agent can add,
whether that's Muse, ChatGPT, Claude, or your own.
It learns from your chats, checks with you when it matters, and shows its receipts.
problem: Your agent remembers you. But it never checks if it's still true.
You can't see what it guessed.
So a guess from two years ago still books your hotel.
And every message, it re-reads a summary of your life. It forgets things, or it costs too much.
idea: Today's agents run on what they guessed about you.
Déjà Vu runs on what you confirmed.
And it asks once, only when a guess is about to book or buy something.
No setup: drop in a ChatGPT, Claude, or Muse export.
demo: Let me show you. Meet Alex, a parent planning a trip.
The chat is just a host.
Watch for the one tap. That tap is the whole product. Over to the demo.
proof: Back to the slides. Here are the eval results: fourteen people, three hundred and twelve checks.
Déjà Vu got eighty percent right. A summary, seventy-two.
When life changed and nobody said so in chat: eighty-one percent, against about half.
And ninety-four percent fewer tokens than re-reading the history.
closer: Agents are great at guessing who you are.
But confirmed memory is always better than inferred memory.
It's live and open source. Try it with your own chat export.
end: What would your agent have booked, if you'd never been asked? Déjà Vu makes sure it's still you. Thank you.
